headline: Fuel price hike: Bus fares rise by 17 paisa per km
summary: Long-distance and city buses in Dhaka and Chattogram will see price increases following a Tk 20 per litre fuel price hike.
details: Bus fares for long-distance routes and public transport in Dhaka and Chattogram have been increased by 17 paisa per kilometre following a fuel price hike.
The decision was finalized at a meeting with transport owners at the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry.
Long-distance bus fares will now rise from Tk 2.23 to Tk 2.40 per kilometre, and metropolitan buses in Dhaka and Chattogram will increase from Tk 2.53 to Tk 2.70 per kilometre.
The government recently raised the prices of diesel, petrol, octane, and kerosene by Tk 20 per litre, with diesel now costing Tk 135 per litre.
Transport owners had initially proposed a 20 paisa per kilometre increase to offset the higher cost of diesel.
This is the latest in a series of adjustments; fares were last revised on April 23 after a Tk 15 per litre diesel price increase.
Inter-district bus fares are based on 52-seat buses, with smaller buses potentially charging more, and road and bridge tolls are added separately.
caption:
Commuters are facing higher costs as bus fares rise by 17 paisa per km following a fuel price hike.

Bus fares for long-distance routes and public transport in Dhaka and Chattogram have been increased by 17 paisa per kilometre following a fuel price hike.

The decision was finalized at a meeting with transport owners at the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry.

Long-distance bus fares will now rise from Tk 2.23 to Tk 2.40 per kilometre, and metropolitan buses in Dhaka and Chattogram will increase from Tk 2.53 to Tk 2.70 per kilometre.

The government recently raised the prices of diesel, petrol, octane, and kerosene by Tk 20 per litre, with diesel now costing Tk 135 per litre.

Transport owners had initially proposed a 20 paisa per kilometre increase to offset the higher cost of diesel.

This is the latest in a series of adjustments; fares were last revised on April 23 after a Tk 15 per litre diesel price increase.

Inter-district bus fares are based on 52-seat buses, with smaller buses potentially charging more, and road and bridge tolls are added separately.

headline_marked: MP Gazi Nazrul's first wife [[gives key info during remand]] in suicide abetment case
headline: MP Gazi Nazrul's first wife gives key info during remand in suicide abetment case
summary: Police say Maksuda Islam provided critical details during interrogation regarding the death of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun.
details: Maksuda Islam, the first wife of MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, has provided important information during her police remand, according to investigators.
Following the interrogation, the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court ordered her to be detained in jail. Police stated that the details gathered will play a helpful role in the ongoing investigation.
The case stems from the death of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, whose body was found hanging from a flat in the NAM Building on September 20.
Mariam's father filed a case alleging abetment of suicide, naming Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Islam, and Mariam's uncle Obaidur Rahman as accused.
During questioning, Maksuda reportedly claimed that Gazi Nazrul and Mariam were married on June 17, allegedly prompted by the accused Obaidur Rahman.
Gazi Nazrul Islam, elected from the Satkhira-4 seat, was expelled from Jamaat-e-Islami in July after a private video involving him and a young woman surfaced online.
Nazrul later identified the woman in the video as his second wife, Mariam Khatun. Obaidur Rahman remains at large.
caption:
Critical revelations emerge as the first wife of MP Gazi Nazrul is interrogated in a suicide abetment case.

Maksuda Islam, the first wife of MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, has provided important information during her police remand, according to investigators.

Following the interrogation, the Chief Judicial Magistrate's court ordered her to be detained in jail. Police stated that the details gathered will play a helpful role in the ongoing investigation.

The case stems from the death of 19-year-old Mariam Khatun, whose body was found hanging from a flat in the NAM Building on September 20.

Mariam's father filed a case alleging abetment of suicide, naming Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Islam, and Mariam's uncle Obaidur Rahman as accused.

During questioning, Maksuda reportedly claimed that Gazi Nazrul and Mariam were married on June 17, allegedly prompted by the accused Obaidur Rahman.

Gazi Nazrul Islam, elected from the Satkhira-4 seat, was expelled from Jamaat-e-Islami in July after a private video involving him and a young woman surfaced online.

Nazrul later identified the woman in the video as his second wife, Mariam Khatun. Obaidur Rahman remains at large.
